chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Bashir, from some of his men, that Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to supplicate with this supplication during every day of the month of Ramadan:

O Allah! This is the month of Ramadan, and this is the month of fasting, and this is the month of turning back (to You), and this is the month of repentance, and this is the month of forgiveness and mercy, and this is the month of emancipation from the Fire and success with Paradise.

O Allah! So preserve it for me and receive it from me, and aid me in it with the best of Your aid, and grant me success in it for obedience to You, and free me therein for Your worship, Your supplication, and recitation of Your Book; and magnify for me therein the blessing, and better for me therein the outcome, and make sound for me therein my body, and expand for me therein my sustenance, and suffice me therein in what concerns me, and answer for me therein my supplication, and cause my hopes to reach fruition therein.

O Allah! Remove from me therein drowsiness, laziness, weariness, slackening, hardness of heart, heedlessness, and delusion. O Allah! Keep from me therein ailments, illnesses, worries, griefs, symptoms, diseases, errors, and sins; and repel from me therein evil, obscenity, hardship, affliction, exhaustion, and toil — for You are the Hearer of supplication.

O Allah! Shelter me therein from the accursed Satan — his whispering, his mocking, his blowing (of evil breath), his puffing (of arrogance), his insinuations, his snares, his deceit, his tricks, his false hopes, his deceptions, his vanity, his strife, his infantry, his traps, his helpers, his followers, his companions, his adherents, his allies, his partners, and all of their schemes.

O Allah! Provide me therein with the completion of its fast and the fulfilment of ambition in its night-prayer, and the perfection of what pleases You therein with patience, faith, certainty, and seeking Your reward; then accept that from us with abundant increase and magnificent recompense.

O Allah! Provide me therein with earnestness, striving, strength, vigor, returning to You, repentance, desire, awe, anxiety, tender-heartedness, truthfulness of tongue, fear of You, hope in You, reliance upon You, trust in You, and abstinence from Your prohibitions — through righteous speech, accepted effort, elevated deeds, and answered supplication; and do not place between me and anything of that an accident, nor illness, nor worry, nor grief — by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.

key_terms.الشَّيْطَان الرَّجِيم: The accursed Satan, the one pelted (rejected from God's mercy)
key_terms.الِاحْتِسَاب: Seeking divine reward, doing deeds with the intention of accountability before God
key_terms.الْإِنَابَة: Turning back to God in contrition; more specific than repentance (tawba), implying returning from heedlessness
key_terms.الْعِتْق: Emancipation, liberation — used metaphorically for release from hellfire
key_terms.الْغِرَّة: Delusion, being deceived into false security
key_terms.الْفَتْرَة: Slackening, a break in religious practice or spiritual motivation
key_terms.الْوَرَع: Scrupulous piety, avoiding the doubtful out of fear of God

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam Zayn al-Abidin recite during Ramadan?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin (AS), the fourth Imam, used this comprehensive supplication every day of Ramadan, covering six dimensions: glorifying the month, requesting assistance for worship, seeking removal of spiritual impediments, seeking protection from Satan, requesting completion of Ramadan's acts of devotion, and asking for inner qualities of piety. This du'a exemplifies the Imam's renowned depth of spirituality — he was known as 'the ornament of worshippers' (Zayn al-'Abidin) — and reflects how the Imams understood Ramadan not merely as a physical fast but as a complete spiritual transformation.
